main_body: A flat snow ground patch: a repeating grey-green field with light-blue drifts and white speckle. It is a terrain tile, not a standing object.
top_band: none: the column scan shows a repeating ground texture (grey-green L~114 with 1-row dark dashes and light-blue patches), not a top band over a front face
evidence: This is a seamless ground surface drawn as a flat top-down texture. It has no standing volume, so the top/front-face contract does not apply. There is no front elevation, side face or raised object, so nothing fails the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The candidate has 7 distinct colours and a median of 7 per tile. That matches the paving reference (7 and 7) but is far below the grass reference (80 colours, 26 per tile). The dark dashes are tinted, with 0% neutral edge pixels, so the outline reads as a material tone. There are no flat fills. The texture is a mechanical repeat of the same speckle and drift motif every 16px, with isolated white dots and dark dashes. It has no per-clump or per-grain variation, so it reads as a stamped pattern, not a hand-shaded snow surface. It looks thinner and more repetitive than the richer grass reference.
